title: Tsunami_Kaiten_Incident_Response_Scenario_e2c
description: Investigate and respond to a potential security incident involving a backdoor trojan with IRC bot capabilities.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The target system has exhibited unusual network activity, including unexpected outbound connections to an unknown server. Initial analysis suggests the presence of a backdoor trojan with IRC bot capabilities. Your task is to investigate and respond to this potential security incident.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the target system with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. The target system is named `target` and has the IP address `192.168.50.5`. Enter the passkey `start` to proceed.
levels.local_content: You have SSH access to the target system with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. The target system is named `target` and has the IP address `192.168.50.5`. Enter the passkey `start` to proceed.

levels.title: Investigate Unusual Network Activity
levels.content: Investigate the unusual network activity on the target system. Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service running on the target system. Submit the name of the suspicious process as the answer.
levels.solution: Check the system logs and running processes for any unusual activity. Use the command `ps aux | grep -i 'suspicious'` to identify the suspicious process running on port 4444. The answer is `ircd`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the system logs and running processes for any unusual activity.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for any unusual network connections or services running on unexpected ports.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command `ps aux | grep -i 'suspicious'` to identify the suspicious process.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot. Identify persistence mechanisms (e.g., systemd, cron, scheduled task). Submit the name of the malicious timer as the answer.
levels.solution: Examine the systemd services and timers to identify the persistence mechanism. Use the command `systemctl list-timers --all` to identify the malicious timer. The answer is `tsunami.timer`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine the systemd services and timers.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for any services or timers that are related to the suspicious activity.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-timers --all` to identify the malicious timer.

levels.title: Identify Lateral Movement
levels.content: Identify file transfers or remote execution used to move between hosts. Correlate events across hosts to identify attacker lateral movement. Submit the name of the file used for lateral movement as the answer.
levels.solution: Check the logs for any file transfers or remote execution commands. Use the command `grep -r 'kaiten' /var/log/` to identify the file used for lateral movement. The answer is `kaiten`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the logs for any file transfers or remote execution commands.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for any commands or services that are used to transfer files or execute commands remotely.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command `grep -r 'kaiten' /var/log/` to identify the file used for lateral movement.
